decision: Base car = 2023 'Scan Data/full car scan.stl' (1YCCwM4M..., 8,255,611 tris), not the 2026 'Ute Scans' export
why: regcheck: the 2026 file sits 0.55 mm median from the 2023 one (same capture re-exported, plus scanned ground and junk behind the car); every 2024 part/state scan registers to both equally (fender outer 2.0 mm, front bumper 3.8 mm, rear bumper inside 4.0-4.5 mm), so the cleaner pre-cropped 2023 export wins

decision: Same-frame scans used at identity: front bumper, front bumper removed, fender and bumper removed, Fender outer, Rear bumper removed, rear bumper inside, front bumper and hood removed (all 2024-11)
why: tools/regcheck.py: 25-88 % of their points within 15 mm of the car at 2-5 mm median (4 mm decimation noise); they were captured in the car's Artec frame

decision: C5 Supplement Hood Open (2025, own frame) registered with FPFH+RANSAC+ICP on the car's front half -> match/hood_open_T.json
why: overlap points sit 2.7 mm median from the car; proj overlay chk/reg_hood.png shows bumper/fenders/headlight pods on the car with the hood swung up - the reference's hood-open beat from real data

decision: Targa Top (2025, own frame) registered with tools/fitpanel.py (8 flip/yaw seeds on the roof + coarse-to-fine ICP) -> match/targa_T.json
why: plain FPFH/RANSAC slid the panel down the windscreen (symmetric curvature); seeded ICP lands it on the roof at 1.6 mm median, centred - chk/reg_targa.png. Removable roof = a C5-specific exploded-view part

decision: Level: one rotation (2.15 deg) from the 2026 export's scanned ground plane applied to every scan (match/level.json, no yaw, nose stays -Y)
why: 2023 export has no ground left to fit; same frame, so the 2026 ground gives the true level. One shared rigid transform keeps all parts registered (same role as prep --like)

decision: Not used: Bumper Light Parts 1-3, headlight/door-card/turn-signal/tab scans, Targa latch/brackets, interior, underside, 'not useful' fenderwells/trunk
why: small parts in their own frames with nothing to register them to at reel scale, or marked not useful by engineering; the reel is whole-car moves + panel explode

decision: Hood opens on a hinge fitted to the captured hood-open scan: axis ~X at y=-2.01 m z=0.86 m (prepped frame), 46 deg (tools/hinge.py, hinge.json, median 3.8 mm)
why: C5 hood is front-hinged; fitting the rotation that lays the scanned open hood back onto the car's closed hood makes the motion and end pose the real captured state, not a guessed pivot

decision: Hood part = full car's own hood skin + the open-hood scan's underside (tools/hoodcombo.py)
why: the rotated open-hood scan alone showed patchy coverage when closed (framing test s6 f1); car skin closed + real underside open reads as one panel

decision: Exploded base = car trimmed under 5 parts (hood, front bumper, Fender outer, rear bumper, targa top) + 'front bumper and hood removed', 'fender and bumper removed', 'front bumper removed', hood-open, 'Rear bumper removed' as captured (tools/composite.py)
why: lesson: use state scans as captured over the full car trimmed back; exposes real engine bay / wheel-well / rear structure; state tris below 70 mm dropped (ground scraps under the sills in the first test)

decision: Rear bumper part = 'rear bumper inside' scan
why: it registers to the car's rear skin (86-87 % within 15 mm) and carries the inner face; there is no separate 'rear bumper' outer scan

decision: Shot plan: s1 front 3/4 low turntable, s2 rear 3/4 orbit, s3 high 3/4 orbit, s4 front wheel ECU (2 mm), s5 quad tail lamps ECU (2 mm), s6 hood opens, s7 top-down spin, s8 explode (staggered: targa, hood, front bumper, fender, rear bumper), s9 float + reassemble, logo
why: brief order (turntables -> close-ups -> hood open -> top-down -> explode/reassemble -> logo) = Temerario ref timeline; no trunk-open shot because the trunk-open scan is marked 'not useful' by engineering

decision: Exploded parts stack above/around the car (offsets 0.4-1.05 m, mostly +Z), camera pulled to 7.6-8.6 m
why: first framing test flew the front bumper and fender out of the 9:16 frame; lesson: keep parts from flying at the lens, float panels above the car like the ref 25-31 s

decision: Shots rendered with 0.5-1 s slack at 75 %/12 spp/15 fps; durations trimmed to the music in project.yaml
why: brief: renders start before the generated track arrives; trimming the out point (never moving the match frame - none here) keeps beats exact

decision: Music = parent session's generated track (c5-corvette_track.mp3, ElevenLabs via Higgsfield), 40.05 s file; kick grid 107.96 BPM, b = 0.5013 + 0.5557k (projects/nissan-frontier/tools/accents.py), ive beats 107.7 BPM
why: brief: only this track; anchored on kick peaks (FG2 lesson), residual 25 ms

per-beat low-band/flux table: intro has no kick until the 9.39 drop (two long Temerario holds there); strongest kicks b16 0.82, b39 0.80, b59 0.81, b61 0.96, b63 0.94; flux peaks b30 1.00 and the b54-b61 build. Holds vary 3-10 beats

decision: Music ends: -16 dB to 36 s, -24 dB 38.0, -35 dB 39.0, -53 dB 39.5 -> video ends 39.40 on the logo, audio fade 1.4 s
why: brief: measure where the generated track ends; parent's estimate 'ends ~38, silent ~39.8' confirmed

decision: s6 hood rises 17.67-20.97 s and is open at the 22.175 kick; s8 panels separate from the 26.621 accent (staggered 0.28 s); s9 last panel (targa) locks home at 34.402 (b61, loudest kick), logo on 35.513 (b63)
why: put the motion on the music's accents; reassembly lock on the heaviest hit, logo on the last big hit before the decay

decision: Each shot renders its cut length + 0.4 s slack; animation keys written in absolute seconds (shots.py fr())
why: slack lets assemble trim the out point without shifting motion timing against the music

decision: s9: from frame 59 (3.916 s = reel 34.43) swap the composite base+parts for the clean full car
why: v1 review of the payoff frame at 34.6 s showed ragged seams on the -X fender/door and rear quarter where the removed-state composite meets the part scans; all scans share one frame, so swapping on the b61 kick where the targa locks reads as the car snapping clean, and the last frame before the logo is the clean scan

decision: v2 shot plan: 9 straight pushes, each framed on one removed area in removal order - front bumper off (hook at 0.6 s) -> bumper inside + exposed crash structure -> fender off on the drop -> fender-mount and nose-structure close-ups -> hood opens on its hinge and lifts off over the engine bay -> THEN rear bumper off (22.175 kick) -> rear bumper inside -> everything home, clean car on 34.402 -> logo; same cut grid as v1
why: reviewer on v1: 'same issue as the other first drafts - focus more specifically on the removed areas and where the useful data is'; sibling notes: rotations are wasted, front first THEN rear, bumpers turn about vertical to show the scanned inside; the useful data is the structure each removed-state scan captured, which v1 only showed in one wide explode

decision: v2 drops the turntables, top-down spin, wheel/tail-lamp close-ups and the targa from the explode
why: they show the outside of the car, which is not the data customers buy; the targa has no roof-off state scan, so it is not shown coming off (honda-civic rule: only parts physically removed with a state scan)

decision: v2 framing fixes: bumpers rise clear of the body before turning about vertical; parked front parts hidden in the hood and rear shots; pushes start closer (A 3.6 m, B 3.6 m, G 3.6 m, I 7.2 m)
why: framing strips showed both bumpers spinning through the body, the parked front bumper as a foreground arc over the engine bay and the hood hovering behind the tail, and the car at ~40 % of frame width

decision: v2 cut grid re-measured on kick onsets: 4.117, 9.309 (drop), 13.689, 17.024, 22.130, 26.471, 30.385, 33.314, 34.402, 35.496 (tools/kickcut.py: zero-phase 40-150 Hz, 8 ms RMS, half-rise from the pre-hit floor)
why: relayed rule: measure cuts against the decoded audio, target half a frame; on the delivered v1 the drop cut was 2.5 frames late and the 13.8/17.2/26.6/30.5 cuts ~4 frames late (those accents are kicks a 16th before the 108 BPM grid line); porsche cutcheck.py's broadband half-rise agrees within 25-40 ms on those but triggers on the guitar elsewhere in this dense mix

decision: v2 final plan implemented from director.md: 6 sections (whole car->front bumper, hood/bay on the drop, -X fender, rear bumper in one held shot, reassembly + fade, 300 px logo), 6 file-name labels, B reused; framing fixes: rear camera +0.7 m (bumper ends clipped), reassembly recentred on the tail with the rear bumper starting near the car
why: parent addendum (user): poor cropping, redundant same-section shots, bumper-removed data highlighted + labeled + shown in detail, states only where scanned; framing strips showed the turned rear bumper clipping both edges and the parked rear bumper as a clipped blob at the left edge of the reassembly

decision: fixed tools/shot.py: use_persistent_data now follows the shot JSON (was hard-coded on); all v2 moving shots render with it off
why: director found the key was ignored; sibling reels lost all lights mid-shot with persistent data on. Reused B was luma-checked: 86 frames, mean 19-29, worst frame-to-frame step 1.5 (no dropout)
